content.text: {"examples":[{"id":"cloud-invite-a-team-member","title":"Create an account and grant it a role, server-side","description":"Creating the account and granting the privilege are two writes, and they are two nodes because only the second one can fail in a way that matters. Create User writes a `_User` row with the authority of the SERVER rather than of whoever called the function, which is what makes this safe to expose as an admin action and also what makes it not Sign Up: it mints no session and returns no session token, so it cannot hand anyone a logged-in session — it creates an account somebody else will later sign in to. Add User To Role then writes the membership row, and `createRole` is deliberately left OFF here. That default is the point of the node: a mistyped role name that silently got created would be a grant that names nobody, because the permission rule that was meant to reference it still says the old, correctly-spelled name — so the account would look privileged in the admin screen and be refused by every access check. Off, a role that does not exist is a `failure` you can see. `Roles` comes back through the same resolver a permission rule's `role:` check evaluates, so what the function returns is the actual state of the access check rather than a second opinion on it. Both writes have a THIRD outcome, and wiring it is what makes re-inviting somebody harmless. `unchanged` on Create User means an account with that username already exists — and it still publishes `userId`, carrying the EXISTING account — so routing it into the grant makes the whole function idempotent in one wire rather than needing a lookup-first branch. `unchanged` on Add User To Role means they were already in it, which is a success for an invite, so it joins the success Response. Leave neither dangling: an unwired third outcome is a chain that silently stops, and the caller waits for a reply that is never sent. If a project's idiom is that a duplicate invite IS a bug, say so explicitly with Treat Unchanged As rather than by leaving the wire off. The failure Response is not optional decoration: a function whose only exit is the success path returns nothing at all when Create User fails, and the caller sees a timeout rather than 'that username is taken'.","demonstrates":["noodl.cloud.createuser","noodl.cloud.addusertorole","noodl.cloud.request","noodl.cloud.response"]},{"id":"bubble-hash-a-value","title":"Turn an email address into a stable fingerprint","description":"The dictionary asks for `:formatted as MD5 hash` and `:formatted as SHA1 Hash`, and the honest answer is that this node offers neither — SHA-256, SHA-384 and SHA-512 only. That is a decision, not a gap: WebCrypto, which Hash runs on in both the browser and a cloud function, does not implement MD5 or SHA-1 for digesting, and hand-rolling one would mean shipping a hash that is broken for every purpose either was ever used for. If you are migrating a Bubble app that stored MD5 fingerprints, they will not reproduce here and no setting will make them; treat that as a re-hash of the source data, not a translation. Two details decide whether this works. Hash is ASYNCHRONOUS — the digest is computed off a later turn than the `Do` that started it — so Digest is wired to the Text and the button is wired to `Do`; reading Digest in the same pass as the click would read the previous answer. And hashing is exact, so the normalisation in front of it is doing real work: `Foo@Example.com ` and `foo@example.com` are different bytes and therefore entirely different digests, which is how a 'stable fingerprint' quietly stops matching. Trim and lower-case first, deliberately, and write down that you did. Failure fires only when WebCrypto is unavailable, which in a browser means the page is not on a secure origin — worth a Log, because the symptom is a blank fingerprint rather than an error. The digest is published as well as rendered: a fingerprint that only ever reaches a Text is a fingerprint nothing can be compared against.","demonstrates":["net.noodl.Hash","Expression","net.noodl.Log","net.noodl.controls.button"]},{"id":"cloud-delete-an-account-and-its-sessions","title":"Delete an account, and the sessions that outlive it","description":"Deleting a user is two deletions, and the ORDER is the interesting part: the sessions go first, then the `_User` row. Reversed, there would be a window in which live session tokens resolve to a row the backend can no longer fetch — signed-in requests from an account that no longer exists. Delete User does both, in that order, with the authority of the server. `sessionsRevoked` reports how many session rows went, which is also the honest answer to 'was anybody actually signed in as them?' — a number worth returning to the caller and worth logging, because it is the difference between deleting a dormant account and cutting somebody off mid-session. `userId` is required: a blank one is a failure with a sentence saying so, and never a fallback to the caller, because the worst possible default for this node is 'delete whoever asked'. `unchanged` means the account was already gone, which is a success for a delete and is wired that way here — an offboarding job that is run twice should not fail the second time. The account id is taken from the request parameters rather than from the caller's own identity precisely so that this is an admin action on someone else; the permission rule on who may call the function is what makes that safe, and it lives on the function, not in this graph.","demonstrates":["noodl.cloud.deleteuser","noodl.cloud.request","noodl.cloud.response","net.noodl.Log"]},{"id":"cloud-revoke-a-role-and-record-it","title":"Take a privilege away, and write down that you did","description":"Revoking is the other half of granting, and it has one behaviour that surprises people: removing a role membership does NOT end that user's existing sessions. They stay signed in; what changes is what the access rules let them do on their next request. If the requirement is 'they are out, now', revoking the role is not sufficient on its own. `unchanged` covers two different post-conditions that both mean 'they are not in it' — they were never a member, or the role does not exist at all — and Error says which. Both are wired into the same continuation here, because for a revoke, 'they are not in that role any more' is the goal and it has been reached either way; a function that failed on an already-revoked user would break every retry. Update User then stamps the account with who did it and when, and it is worth being clear why that is a different node from Set User Properties: that one writes to whoever is signed in and fails when nobody is, while this writes to the account whose id you give it with the authority of the server. `userId` is required and a blank one is a failure rather than a fallback to the caller — which is exactly the accident (editing the admin instead of the target) that the split exists to prevent. Get User Roles reads the result back through the same resolver the permission check uses, so the Response tells the screen what the access rules will actually agree to, not what this function believes it just did.","demonstrates":["noodl.cloud.removeuserfromrole","noodl.cloud.updateuser","noodl.cloud.getuserroles","noodl.cloud.request"]},{"id":"cloud-who-is-in-this-role","title":"Show the member list for a role, a page at a time","description":"Get User Roles answers 'which roles is this user in'. List Users In Role answers the other direction — 'who is in this role' — and that direction is the one an ordinary membership screen needs. Both walk the same junction, so neither can disagree with what a permission rule's `role:` check would say. Paging is done with Limit and Skip rather than by fetching everything and slicing in the browser, because the member list of a role is exactly the collection that is small in development and large in production; Skip is computed from the page number in an Expression so the arithmetic lives in one place. `Total` is the count for the WHOLE role, not the page, which is what a pager needs to know how many pages there are — a function that returns only the rows cannot render '3 of 47'. `unchanged` fires instead of `done` when the role is empty or does not exist, and it is wired to the same Response here on purpose: an empty member list is a perfectly good answer to send back, and leaving that outcome dangling would make a brand-new role look like a broken function to the caller. Read-only throughout — nothing on this path writes, so it is safe to call on every render of the screen.","demonstrates":["noodl.cloud.listusersinrole","noodl.cloud.request","noodl.cloud.response","Expression"]},{"id":"cloud-check-a-webhook-and-a-token","title":"Prove an inbound request really came from who it says","description":"Two different 'is this genuine' questions, side by side, because choosing the wrong one is the common mistake. HMAC is for a webhook: the sender computed a keyed digest of the body with a shared secret and put it in a header, and you recompute it and compare. The input that decides whether this works is Value — it must be the RAW body, byte for byte, exactly as it arrived. Re-serialising the parsed object first produces a different string (key order, whitespace, number formatting) and therefore a different signature, and the symptom is every webhook failing verification with no clue why. JWT Verify is for a token somebody else ISSUED to you, and it refuses any token whose header names an algorithm other than the one you selected — which is what defeats both `alg: none` and algorithm confusion, and is why Algorithm is set here rather than read from the token. Nothing inside a token may be believed before the signature check, so Claims is left alone on failure rather than handed over unchecked; reading claims off a token you have not verified is the same bug as trusting the webhook body. Clock Tolerance exists for issuers whose clock is not quite yours and defaults to 0. Both keys come from Secret nodes by name, so neither credential is in the graph. Note what neither node is for: your own users' sessions. That is Verify Session Token, which asks this backend about its own `_Session` rows.","demonstrates":["noodl.cloud.hmac","noodl.cloud.jwtverify","noodl.cloud.secret","noodl.cloud.response"]},{"id":"cloud-sign-a-token-with-a-stored-secret","title":"Mint a signed token for another service to check","description":"The key never appears in the graph — only the NAME of the secret does, which is what makes this function safe to commit and safe to export. Secret resolves that name against the backend's machine-local `secrets.json` and then against a `NODEGX_SECRET_<NAME>` environment variable, and it reaches the project author's own credentials only: the backend's own webhook, email, auth and admin credentials are not addressable from a graph at all. Signing is cloud-only for the obvious reason — a browser node with a key input would be a browser holding the key. Two things about the token itself. A JWT is SIGNED, NOT ENCRYPTED: everything in Claims is readable by anyone who holds the token, so it carries identifiers and never secrets, and 'nobody will look' is not a security property. And `exp` is stamped only when Expires In is set — `iat` is always stamped, `exp` is not — so a token with no expiry is something you chose rather than something that happened to you. Ten minutes is set here because this token exists to be handed to one other service for one call. The chain is Do-driven throughout: Secret publishes Value on `done`, and only then is there a key to sign with, so the signature is wired to fire from that signal rather than from the request. Failure is a single Response, because a function that cannot read its secret and a function that cannot sign look identical from the caller's side and neither should return a token-shaped blank.","demonstrates":["noodl.cloud.secret","noodl.cloud.jwtsign","noodl.cloud.request","noodl.cloud.response"]},{"id":"cloud-tag-a-feed-item-with-a-model","title":"Tag each new feed item with a model, and store it once","description":"The per-item half of a feed reader, server-side: ask a model for the item's topics in a shape you can rely on, then write the row so that seeing the same item again updates it instead of duplicating it. Five things here are decisions rather than plumbing. First, the key is a NAME — Api Key Secret says MODEL_KEY, and the value lives in the backend's secrets, so the key is never a port value, never in the exported workflow, and never in an execution record. Second, Base Url comes out of a Secret node rather than being typed into the graph, so pointing this at a gateway or a test double is an operator's edit and not an author's. Third, Output Schema is wired from a Function node, not typed: it is an object, and the port only accepts a connection. With it set, Json carries the parsed answer in exactly the shape you asked for, and Text carries the raw JSON of it — which is why the little Function after the model reads Json and joins the list into one readable string rather than storing a blob. Fourth, Create Record's Upsert On names 'id', the feed item's own identity, which Parse Feed guarantees is never empty. The collection must declare that column and a UNIQUE index on it; with the index the second poll updates one row, without it the second poll fails. Fifth, and least decorative, every failure path is wired to a Failed output: a missing secret, a refusal, a script that threw, a write the index refused. This fragment is a Run Tasks task template, and a task that never reaches a completion output is one the loop waits for forever — so the function does not fail, it hangs until its timeout. Note also the Run On Value Change boxes: with a control signal wired, an input that is still ticked runs the node a SECOND time, early, with everything else unset. Every value input here is fed by the signal that should consume it, so every one of them is unticked.","demonstrates":["noodl.cloud.modelrequest","noodl.cloud.secret","NewDbModelProperties","JavaScriptFunction","Component Inputs","Component Outputs"]},{"id":"community-csv-download","title":"Turn rows into a file the browser downloads","description":"Two `JavaScriptFunction` nodes in series and no backend anywhere: the first folds an array of objects into CSV text, the second wraps that text in a `Blob` and hands `URL.createObjectURL` the result, and `External Link` opens it. That URL is the whole trick — it is a real, fetchable address that exists only inside this tab, so the download never leaves the browser and nothing has to be uploaded first. ⚠️ Compare it with `net.noodl.ToCSV` before reusing the conversion half: the built-in node handles quoting and embedded delimiters, which hand-rolled CSV usually does not. The half worth copying is the object-URL download.","demonstrates":["Component Inputs","JavaScriptFunction","net.noodl.externallink"]},{"id":"community-email-signup-validat","title":"Check an email is well-formed and not already taken","description":"Sign-up validation as a chain of small truths rather than one function: an `Expression` says the field is non-empty, a `JavaScriptFunction` says it looks like an address, and a `DbCollection2` query says nobody has it yet — and an `And` node combines them into the one boolean the button enables on. The `Timer` in front of the query is the detail worth copying: it debounces, so the database is asked once the typing stops instead of once per keystroke. ⚠️ The two `Inverter` nodes read as clutter until you notice what they buy — 'no user came back' is the success case here, and inverting it keeps every input to the `And` meaning 'this is fine', which is what makes the combination readable at all.","demonstrates":["And","DbCollection2","Expression","Group","Inverter","JavaScriptFunction","Text","Timer","net.noodl.controls.button","net.noodl.controls.textinput"]},{"id":"community-web-rtc-video-record","title":"Record video from the camera and store the result","description":"The same shape as the audio recorder and worth reading beside it, because what the two have in common is the part that generalises: ask for the device, gate every control on the answer, let one `Javascript2` node own the `MediaRecorder`, and convert the finished `Blob` before anything tries to store it. Video adds the preview problem — you need a live `<video>` element while recording and a playable one afterwards — which is why a Custom HTML node holds the player rather than an `Image`. ⚠️ `getUserMedia` requires a secure origin: this works on `localhost` and over HTTPS and fails on a plain-HTTP deploy, which is a deployment fault that presents as a permission one.","demonstrates":["Component Inputs","Component Outputs","Expression","Group","Inverter","JavaScriptFunction","Javascript2","NewDbModelProperties","States","Text","module.inlineHtml","net.noodl.controls.button"]},{"id":"fn-play-audio-a-cloud-function-returns","title":"Speak a phrase: text-to-speech in a cloud function, played in the page as it came","description":"A text-to-speech (TTS) API is called from a cloud function, so its key stays on the server, and the page plays what comes back. Three decisions matter. First, the key is a NAME: Secret reads GEMINI_API_KEY from the backend's secrets, the Function sends it in the x-goog-api-key header (never in the URL, which ends up in logs), and the key is never a port value the page can see. Second, and the one that is easy to get wrong: the audio an API returns today is almost always a FINISHED FILE (WAV, MP3 or OGG, with its own header, and sometimes extra chunks after the samples), so the cloud function passes the base64 and its MIME type through untouched and the page plays it as it is. Only a MIME type that says raw samples (audio/L16 or audio/pcm, which older Gemini text-to-speech returned) needs a WAV header put around it. Wrapping a finished file in a second header plays its first header as a click and anything after the samples as half a second of loud static. Gemini's current text-to-speech model returns audio/wav, so the wrap branch does not run for it. Third, failures stay readable: a script that threw answers through a failure Response with its own message, and a missing secret answers with a fixed sentence, because the Secret's own error names a server path the page should not show. Playback is a Function calling `new Audio(...)`, run from the call's Done; the call starts from a press, so the browser allows sound. In this function the value inputs have Run On Value Change unticked, because a signal runs each Function.","demonstrates":["CloudFunction2","noodl.cloud.request","noodl.cloud.secret","noodl.cloud.response","JavaScriptFunction"]}]}

content.text: {"id":"cloud-invite-a-team-member","title":"Create an account and grant it a role, server-side","description":"Creating the account and granting the privilege are two writes, and they are two nodes because only the second one can fail in a way that matters. Create User writes a `_User` row with the authority of the SERVER rather than of whoever called the function, which is what makes this safe to expose as an admin action and also what makes it not Sign Up: it mints no session and returns no session token, so it cannot hand anyone a logged-in session — it creates an account somebody else will later sign in to. Add User To Role then writes the membership row, and `createRole` is deliberately left OFF here. That default is the point of the node: a mistyped role name that silently got created would be a grant that names nobody, because the permission rule that was meant to reference it still says the old, correctly-spelled name — so the account would look privileged in the admin screen and be refused by every access check. Off, a role that does not exist is a `failure` you can see. `Roles` comes back through the same resolver a permission rule's `role:` check evaluates, so what the function returns is the actual state of the access check rather than a second opinion on it. Both writes have a THIRD outcome, and wiring it is what makes re-inviting somebody harmless. `unchanged` on Create User means an account with that username already exists — and it still publishes `userId`, carrying the EXISTING account — so routing it into the grant makes the whole function idempotent in one wire rather than needing a lookup-first branch. `unchanged` on Add User To Role means they were already in it, which is a success for an invite, so it joins the success Response. Leave neither dangling: an unwired third outcome is a chain that silently stops, and the caller waits for a reply that is never sent. If a project's idiom is that a duplicate invite IS a bug, say so explicitly with Treat Unchanged As rather than by leaving the wire off. The failure Response is not optional decoration: a function whose only exit is the success path returns nothing at all when Create User fails, and the caller sees a timeout rather than 'that username is taken'.","demonstrates":["noodl.cloud.createuser","noodl.cloud.addusertorole","noodl.cloud.request","noodl.cloud.response"],"components":[{"name":"/Cloud Functions/Invite Team account","parameters":{"emailVerified":false}},{"id":"grant","type":"noodl.cloud.addusertorole","label":"Grant the role — createRole stays off on A change is laid over what that row already had, then checked as a whole. - `removeChange`: takes a change back (the row returns to how the game ships it). - **Checked over HTTP**, not just deployed: a child's account gets `notGrownup`; "M3RDE", ``, 100 000 stars, an unknown field and a made-up table are refused with a reason; a good change is saved and a second one merges into it. - **Got wrong, and it mattered:** the backend starts in *dev-open* mode, where permission rules are reported but not enforced — my "nobody may write" rule let a child's account write 9 999 stars straight into the collection. The in-graph role check stays as a second lock. EOF

nodes.label: words (shared on purpose)
nodes.comment: Shared on purpose: every view Function reads the same words.

nodes.label: The game's fonts
nodes.comment: The three Google fonts the coded game used (index.html). Offline the system fonts in the tokens take over.

nodes.label: gala: the save, kept on this device
nodes.comment: Persisted in this browser's localStorage, as the coded game's save was. The grown-ups' changes are NOT here: they live in the backend so they survive a cleared browser.

nodes.label: ui: what is on screen now
The grown-ups' changes
nodes.comment: Read once when the game opens. Unfiltered on purpose: every saved change applies.

nodes.label: Don't wait for the backend for ever
nodes.comment: If the backend cannot be reached the game still opens, with the tables as they ship.

nodes.label: Lay the grown-ups' changes over the game
nodes.comment: Every change is checked again in the browser (settings/check.js) before gala-rules' applyRows lays it over the tables, once per visit.

nodes.label: Open the save
nodes.comment: After the changes are laid over the tables (a new school starts with the grown-ups' stars). Repairs an old save, or starts a fresh one. Once.

toolu_01LfEQNPQb99qP8YXbFwVt7R.description: What happens when the game opens: the words of both languages, the two stores (the save, kept on this device, and the screen state), the grown-ups' changes laid over the game's tables, then the save opened and repaired. Sets the Variable "ready" when the game may draw.

nodes.label: words (shared on purpose)
nodes.comment: Shared on purpose: every view Function reads the same words.

nodes.label: The game's fonts
nodes.comment: The three Google fonts the coded game used (index.html). Offline the system fonts in the tokens take over.

nodes.label: gala: the save, kept on this device
nodes.comment: Persisted in this browser's localStorage, as the coded game's save was. The grown-ups' changes are NOT here: they live in the backend so they survive a cleared browser.

nodes.label: ui: what is on screen now
The grown-ups' changes
nodes.comment: Read once when the game opens. Unfiltered on purpose: every saved change applies.

nodes.label: Don't wait for the backend for ever
nodes.comment: If the backend cannot be reached the game still opens, with the tables as they ship.

nodes.label: Lay the grown-ups' changes over the game
nodes.comment: Every change is checked again in the browser (settings/check.js) before gala-rules' applyRows lays it over the tables, once per visit.

nodes.label: Open the save
nodes.comment: After the changes are laid over the tables (a new school starts with the grown-ups' stars). Repairs an old save, or starts a fresh one. Once.

content.text: Start-up logic in place. Now the 3D stage component — the Group that hosts three.js's canvas and the Function that runs it:

input.description: The school in 3D behind everything: the stage, the dressing room, the car park, the dancers and the music. The three.js code (scripts/stage) draws into its own canvas inside this Group; the graph tells it the save and the screen state, and it reports the live evening, the camera, taps and the floating toolbar's place.

nodes.label: 3D view
nodes.comment: Fills the window behind the sheet and the bars. The canvas three.js makes is put in here and nowhere else.

nodes.label: 3D stage
nodes.comment: No node draws three.js or synthesises music, so this stays code: reference/src world/people/play/music, as factories in scripts/stage. three.js itself is the vendored r177 in assets/vendor. It runs once, when the Group is on the page.

nodes.label: Tell the stage
nodes.comment: Whenever the save or the screen state changes, the 3D catches up (the coded game's G was shared; here the stage keeps its own copy).

nodes.label: Stop the 3D when the page goes

parameters.functionScript: if (Inputs.stage && Inputs.stage.unmount) Inputs.stage.unmount();

nodes.label: What the press changes
nodes.comment: Runs only on a press (every input's Run On Value Change is off). scripts/game/dispatch.js decides; this writes nothing itself, it hands the answer to the Set Global Store nodes.

### 8. State and start-up: `state.js` + `main.js`'s start → `Logic/Start Up`, two Global Stores, one dispatcher

- **Was:** `load()` from localStorage into `G.S`, `save()` after every change, `G` also holding the screen state.
- **Became:**
  - Global Store **`gala`**, persisted (`storageKey: gala-game-v2`), key `save` — the child's save, on this device,
    as before. I checked persistence across a reload with a two-button test page first.
  - Global Store **`ui`**, not persisted: `ui` (tab, screen, picks), `live` (the evening as it plays, written four
    times a second by the 3D stage), `res` (the rules' answer for the evening), `cam`, `float`, `toast`. Splitting
    `live` from `ui` matters: only the run sheet and the clock subscribe to it, so the tabs don't recompute four
    times a second.
  - **`Logic/Start Up`** (in the App, beside the Router): the Words Static Data → a Variable; Query Records on
    `GameChange` → "Lay the grown-ups' changes over the game" (checks each row again, then gala-rules'
    `applyRows`, once) → "Open the save" (repairs or creates it — a new school gets the grown-ups' starting stars)
    → Variable `ready`, which mounts the Game page. A Delay of 4 s lets the game open with the shipped tables if
    the backend can't be reached.
  - **`Game/Dispatcher`**: one Receive Event on `gala-act` → one Function (`game/dispatch.js`) → Set Global Store
    nodes. Every button in every tab is a Send Event with a fixed `act` (`order:up`, `form:addMove`, `go`) and
    the row's id as `arg`. This is the coded `changed()`, spread out: the graph shows which button sends what.
- **Got wrong:** "Open the save" writes the store it reads, and NodeGX stopped it with *Cyclic loop detected*;
  unticking Run On Value Change for the store input fixed it. A view Function ran once before the save existed
  and threw; every view now starts with `if (!Inputs.save || !Inputs.save.school) return;`.

### 9. The screen: `index.html` + `ui.js` painters → `Pages/Game` and its sections

- `Game/Stage 3D` (the 3D Group and its Functions), `Game/Top Bar`, `Game/Camera Bar`, `Game/Sheet` (tabs row,
  scrolling body, buttons row), `Game/Toast` (a Switch and a 2.6 s Delay), `Game/Season Letter` (the modal),
  `Game/Furniture Toolbar` (the coded `#float`, placed by the 3D stage's `float` output), `Game/Live`,
  `Game/Results`, and the eight tabs `Tabs/Order`, `Formation`, `Gouter`, `Costumes`, `Build`, `Parking`, `Shop`,
  `Notebook`. Each tab: one Subscribe per store key it needs, one view Function, Texts and Repeaters, and a Send
  Event per kind of press. The sheet mounts the tab whose `show_<tab>` is true.
- **Driven like a child arrives** (`drive_page` from the start page, no page named): the season letter, "C'est
  parti !", every tab, ▼ on a programme card (the order changed), a dress rehearsal (live clock in the top bar),
  "Aller à la fin", the verdicts and a "Pourquoi ?" opened, back, gala night: **96 ⭐, 30 → 126**, and the
  notebook's entry. No console errors at the end.
- **Didn't map cleanly:**
  - `confirm()` (delete a block, start again) and `prompt()` (rename a block) are browser dialogs, not elements;
    they became an inline "are you sure?" box and an inline Text Input, driven by `ui.confirm` / `ui.renaming`.
  - Drag-to-reorder of programme cards (pointer tracking over `getBoundingClientRect`) — the cards keep their ▲▼
    buttons, which the coded game also had; dragging them is gone. The hint now says "move the cards up or down".
  - The enlarged plan pop-over (`#planpop`, built with `createElement`) and the ruler are not rebuilt.
  - Sizes: a percentage sent as a string ("48.5%") is refused by a Group's width; it wants a number in the
    port's unit. Two components had that wrong and the browser console said so.

EOF

content.text: Now the grown-ups' page itself — sign-in, the one-time claim, and the editor, all calling the checked cloud functions:

input.description: The grown-ups' settings: sign in (the first account made here becomes the home's grown-up, and nobody after it can), then change the game's tables — names, difficulty, prices, minutes, a new school's stars — add a new step or a new costume, or take a change back. Every change is saved through the checked cloud function and is kept on the game's backend, not in this browser.

### 10. The grown-ups' settings page (new): `Pages/Grownups`

- **Built from:** a User node, Log In / Sign Up / Log Out, three Cloud Function nodes (`claimGrownup`,
  `saveChange`, `removeChange`), a Query Records on `GameChange`, a Repeater of `Grownups/Row Editor` (names in
  both languages, and the table's numbers: difficulty and counts for a step, price and minutes for a costume…),
  `Grownups/New Step` and `Grownups/New Costume` (Text Inputs and `UI/Labelled Pick` dropdowns — the server
  refused six hand-copied label+dropdown boxes and asked for one component, rightly), the stars box, and a
  `Grownups/Words` Static Data. Four small Functions: what the page shows, the change to send (one check run in
  the browser first so a grown-up hears *why* at once), the stars, and the error sentence.
- **Driven from the game's start page:** ⚙︎ → sign in as the test grown-up → "M3RDE" as a step name → refused
  with the reason, nothing saved → "Plié royal" → *Enregistré ✓* → a new costume "Pirate" → 80 stars for a new
  school → "Open the game with the changes" → **"Plié royal" is in the step palette, "Pirate" in the costumes**.
  A fresh browser (nothing in localStorage) opens a school with **80 ⭐**. A second account ("petitmalin") is
  told it is not the grown-ups' account, and the editor never mounts.
- **Why it lasts:** the changes are rows in the backend, laid over gala-rules' tables by `applyRows` each time the
  game opens. Clearing the browser loses only the child's save; another computer reading the same backend sees
  the same changes; a new version of the game ships new default tables and the same rows are laid over them
  (a row whose id the new version no longer knows is refused by the checker and simply skipped).
- **Didn't map cleanly:** a Repeater re-publishes a row's value outputs, but the value it holds is the last row
  that *changed* one, not the row whose button was pressed — so typing in row A then saving row B would have sent
  A's text with B's id. The row now packs its own values into one object at the moment its Save is pressed. And
  the Log Out node's trigger is called `login` (the server said so).

EOF

input.command:
cd /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-richardosborne-vscode-projects-OpenNoodl/9a20b9d4-b667-4608-b022-ebbacfd44fee/scratchpad/own023-r2b/rounds/B2/work/gala; cat >> CONVERSION.md <<'EOF'
### 11. Clean-up after testing

My tests left three accounts and three changes in the backend. I took the changes back through `removeChange`,
took the test account out of the `grownup` role, and gave the three test accounts long random passwords nobody
knows (the backend has no delete-user tool I could reach). Nobody holds the `grownup` role now: **the first
account the real grown-up creates on the settings page becomes the grown-ups' account** — do that before the
children find the ⚙︎.

---

## At the end

### What was easy

- **The rules.** They were already pure, so "convert" meant a 30-line copier and an equality check.
- **Rows → Repeaters.** Every `.map(...).join('')` in `ui.js` became a For Each over the same rows, and the 25 row
  components were quick once `UI/Chip` had settled the pattern (Component Inputs → States → Component Outputs).
- **State.** A persisted Global Store *is* the localStorage save, with change notification for free.
- **One dispatcher.** Send Event (`act`, `arg`) from every button into one Receive Event made 60-odd different
  presses manageable, and it reads well on the canvas.
- **The server.** Every refused write named the port, the reason and usually the fix. I never had a write
  silently accepted that then didn't work, except the dimension-as-string case (caught by the console).

### What was hard

- **Volume.** `ui.js` is 752 dense lines; as nodes it is 54 components and 762 nodes. Each tab is one large
  `create_component` call of 30–90 nodes, and a big page has to be resent whole to change it.
- **Things a string of HTML does for free:** the SVG stage plan (now Groups placed in pixels plus Drag nodes),
  `<details>` (a Switch), `<b>` in a sentence (dropped), `confirm()`/`prompt()` (inline boxes),
  `scrollIntoView` on the step being danced (not rebuilt).
- **Two copies of state.** The 3D code wants to read the state every frame; the graph wants to own it. `sync()`
  in, `emit()` out works, but it is the one seam where a bug could hide.
- **Security defaults.** The backend started in dev-open mode; a "nobody may write" rule wasn't enforced until I
  switched enforcement on. Without testing the direct write over HTTP I would have shipped it open.
- **Speed in the test browser.** In the headless browser (software WebGL, no GPU) each tap takes 3–7 s to
  settle; JavaScript is only ~5 ms a frame, the rest is the 3D scene drawn without a GPU. The coded game draws the
  same scene. I couldn't measure on real hardware from here.

### What was lost or changed

- Lost: bold words inside sentences; dragging programme cards (the ▲▼ buttons remain); the ruler and the enlarged
  stage plan; scrolling the try-out list to the step being danced; the bottom-sheet layout on narrow screens
  (the sheet stays a 400 px side panel); `window.__game`, the coded game's handle for its own test driver; the
  import of a round-1 save from another origin.
- Changed: the programme hint says "move the cards up or down"; renaming a block and the two confirmations are
  inline; the school name is checked like a grown-up's name (a rude name is refused with a toast).
- Added: the grown-ups' settings, the backend, the checker in two places, the ⚙︎ in the top bar.
- Fonts: as before, Fredoka/Nunito/Playball come from Google Fonts when online; offline the system fonts take over.

### How much is nodes, how much is code

Counted from the project files (`components/**/nodes.json`, `scripts/**`):

| | count |
|---|---|
| components | 54 (UI 26, Tabs 8, Game 11, Grownups 5, Logic 1, pages 2, cloud functions 3) |
| nodes | **762**, of which 363 draw (Group, Text, controls, Repeaters…) and 74 are Send Events |
| code nodes | **33** Function nodes (no Expression, no Script node) — 4.3 % of the nodes; the server's own measure says "95.1 % known" |
| lines inside those Functions | 390, most of them `Outputs.x = v.x` lines handing rows to Repeaters, plus the ~200-line checker pasted into `saveChange` |
| script files | 21 files, 3 369 lines: **2 112 are generated copies** (gala-rules 990, the 3D/music modules 1 014, the checker 108) and **1 257 hand-written** (view rows 585, actions/dispatch/save/text 462, the 3D glue 189, settings 21) |

So: every screen, tab, list, button, label, dialog, message and the game's state are nodes; the code is the rules
(unchanged), the 3D view and the music (the reference's own modules), and the layer that turns the save into
rows and a press into a new save. The words are data in two Static Data nodes (389 game rows, 66 grown-up rows).

### How to see it

`npx @nodegx/preview app --open` (from this folder) — it starts the game's backend too. The game opens on the
season's letter; the grown-ups' settings are behind ⚙︎ in the top bar. `node tools/check-rules.mjs` and
`node tools/check-views.mjs` re-check the code layers; `node tools/sync-rules.mjs` / `sync-stage.mjs` /
`sync-check.mjs` regenerate the copies when gala-rules or the checker changes.
EOF
wc -l CONVERSION.md

# Converting "Le Gala de danse" to NodeGX — the log The coded game is in `reference/` (plain ES modules + three.js r177). The NodeGX app is in `app/`. The rules (`gala-rules/`) are shared, unchanged. ## Before I started ### How I read the existing code I read it in the order the game runs: `index.html` (the page: a canvas, a top bar, a camera bar, a side sheet with tabs/body/"go" bar, a float toolbar, a toast and a modal), `main.js` (start-up, the frame loop, pointer and keys on the canvas), `state.js` (one shared object `G`: the save `G.S` in localStorage `gala-game-v2` plus what is on screen now: screen, tab, picked number, the run…), then `ui.js` (752 lines: every tab is a `paint…()` function that builds an HTML string and sets `innerHTML`, then binds `onclick`s that mutate `G.S.plan` / `G.S.school` and call `changed()` = save + re-simulate + repaint everything), `i18n.js` (every sentence, FR/EN, many of them functions with plurals and ``), and finally the code that draws and sounds: `world.js` (three.js school, stage, loge, car park, camera), `people.js` (dancers), `play.js` (plays the engine's schedule over time, emits "say" lines), and `music.js` (Web Audio synth that follows the run). The rules are already pure: `engine.js`, `data.js`, `plan.js`, `tunes.js` have no DOM and are byte-identical in `reference/src` and `gala-rules/src` (I diffed them). What I learned that drives the plan: 1. The UI is **"state → whole HTML string → innerHTML"** on every change. There is no component model: the "card", "chip", "stepper", "shop row", "verdict" are string helpers. Each one becomes a NodeGX component, and each `.map(...).join('')` becomes a Repeater (`For Each`) over an array. 2. All mutation goes through `changed()`, which means **one** shared store. That maps onto a NodeGX **Global Store** (with `persist` on for the save), so every component reads the same state without wires. 3. The 3D and the sound read `G` directly every frame. They can't become nodes (nothing in NodeGX draws three.js or synthesises audio), so they stay code — but they must stop reading `G`: the graph will *push* the state to them. 4. `i18n.js` mixes words with logic (plurals, ``, conditionals). The words can be data; the logic that picks them stays in the code that builds each row. ### The plan: what becomes what | coded part | becomes in NodeGX | why | |---|---|---| | `index.html` layout, `style.css` look | `Pages/Game`: Groups for the top bar, camera bar, side sheet, toast, intro dialog; the project's design tokens set to the theatre palette (plum, gold, velvet) | every visible element must be a node | | `state.js` (`G.S`, save/load/mend) | a persisted **Global Store** `save` (the save) + a non-persisted Global Store `ui` (tab, screen, picks); a small "Mend save" Function on start-up that calls `gala-rules/plan.js` | state must live in nodes; the mend calls rules code | | `ui.js` tab painters | one component per tab (`Tabs/Order`, `Tabs/Formation`, `Tabs/Gouter`, `Tabs/Costumes`, `Tabs/Build`, `Tabs/Parking`, `Tabs/Shop`, `Tabs/Notebook`), the run sheet, the results | one named section = one component | | string helpers (`stepper`, `card`, chips, `facts`, meters, shop `row`, verdict `card`) | shared components in `UI/` (Chip, Stepper, Fact, Meter, OrderCard, ItemButton, ShopRow, Verdict…), drawn by Repeaters | repetition is data | | `onclick` handlers that mutate the plan | each row publishes a click; the tab wires it to a small Function that returns the new plan, written back with **Set Global Store** | the nested plan edit (splice a card, clamp a time) is the code part; the wiring is nodes | | `i18n.js` words | a **Static Data** table of words (key, fr, en) in the App, read by the view Functions; the sentences with numbers in them are templates in that table | words are data, not code | | `engine.js` / `data.js` / `plan.js` / `tunes.js` | **project script files** `scripts/rules/*.js`, generated mechanically from `gala-rules/src` (only `import`/`export` lines rewritten to the script-file form); called from Functions with `Scripts.engine.simulate(…)` | the brief says to use them as they are; NodeGX script files are CommonJS-style, so a generator keeps them identical | | `world.js`, `people.js`, `play.js`, `music.js` (three.js, Web Audio) | script files wrapped as factories that receive `THREE`, `window` and `document` from one **Function** node ("3D stage"), which mounts the renderer's canvas in a Group | no node draws 3D or makes sound; the brief allows this | | `main.js` pointer handling on the canvas | stays inside the 3D code (it is input *on the canvas*) and reports taps to the graph as events | | | run playback's feed / toasts / "done" | the 3D code sends **events** (`Noodl.Events`) that **Receive Event** nodes turn into store writes | the graph, not the code, decides what the screen shows | | `confirm()` / `prompt()` dialogs | NodeGX popups / inline Text Input | browser dialogs are not nodes | | the grown-ups' settings (new) | `Pages/Grownups` + a backend collection `GameChange` + cloud functions that check every change | must survive a cleared browser and another computer; a child must not be able to bypass the checks | ### What stays code, and why - the rules (gala-rules), called from Functions — required by the brief; - the three.js view and its pointer handling, and the Web Audio music — no node does this; - small Functions that turn the save + the rules' answer into rows for the Repeaters, and the plan edits. Everything a row *shows* is a node; the Function only decides *which* rows and *what text*. ### Safety, decided up front - The settings page needs a grown-up account. The first account made claims the `grownup` role; after that, no other account can (checked in a cloud function, not in the page). - Writes go only through a cloud function that accepts known tables and known fields, clamps every number to a sensible range, accepts names only as short plain text from a word filter (FR + EN), and picks icons/styles/themes only from lists the game already knows. The collection itself is closed to direct writes. - The browser checks the same rules again before laying a change over the game, so a bad row can never reach the screen even if it got into the database some other way. --- ## As I went ### 1. Checking the unknowns before building anything Before converting a single screen I built a throw-away page with one Group, one Function and two Texts to answer four questions the plan depended on. All four answered yes, in the headless preview (`drive_page`): - a Function can use the rules as project script files (`uses: rules/engine`) — `simulate()` returned 91 points; - a Group's `this` output gives the Function its DOM element (to host the 3D canvas); - three.js loads from the project's `assets/vendor/` with a dynamic `import()` (r177, no build step); - a Function can still set its outputs *after* it has returned (from a timer or an animation frame), and `Noodl.Events.emit` reaches a Receive Event. So the 3D code can report the evening back into the graph. Wrong the first time: I passed the Function's `uses` as a JSON array; NodeGX wants one comma-separated string. And a `String` node has `saveValue`, not `set`. The server refused both writes and named the fix, so nothing broke. ### 2. The rules: `gala-rules/src/*.js` → `app/scripts/rules/*.js` - **Was:** four ES modules with `import`/`export`. - **Became:** four NodeGX script files. NodeGX script files are CommonJS-style (`exports`, and `use('rules/data')` to reach another file), so `tools/sync-rules.mjs` copies the files and rewrites only the `import`/`export` lines. Every other line is gala-rules' own. `tools/check-rules.mjs` loads the copy the way NodeGX does and checks it plays exactly the same evening as gala-rules for 4 seasons × 3 modes, and the same tunes. `npm test` in `gala-rules/` still passes; I changed nothing there. - **Didn't map cleanly:** "use them as they are" and "NodeGX script files have no `import`" pull in opposite directions. A generator + an equality check is my answer: the rules are byte-for-byte the same apart from module syntax, and re-running one command picks up a new gala-rules. ### 3. The words: `i18n.js` → a Static Data table + one small template filler - **Was:** an object of ~350 FR/EN entries, a third of them functions (`(n) => \`${n} poste${n > 1 ? 's' : ''}\``), some with `` inside. - **Became:** 389 rows `{ key, fr, en }` for a **Static Data** node (`tools/extract-words.mjs` produced them by calling each sentence function with `{0}`, `{1}`… as its arguments). Plurals became `{0:s}`, lower-casing `{0:lower}`; the ~25 functions with real logic (a sentence that changes with the floor, the season, a count) became two rows each (`say_floorSwap_bois` / `_tapis`), written by hand. `scripts/game/text.js` (56 lines) fills a template and formats times, durations and numbers. - **Lost:** the bold words inside sentences (`21 h`). A Text node draws plain text, and building HTML is exactly what the brief rules out. The sentences read the same; the emphasis is gone. ### 4. The screens' logic: `ui.js` → `scripts/view/*.js` (rows) and `scripts/game/actions.js` (presses) - **Was:** 752 lines in which each tab's painter computes what to show, *and* writes it as an HTML string, *and* binds the clicks, *and* mutates the plan inside the click handler. - **Became:** two halves of code, so the third — the screen — can be nodes: - `view/frame.js`, `view/prep.js`, `view/formation.js`, `view/run.js`: one function per tab that returns plain rows (`{ id, label, pressed, dot }` for a chip, `{ id, name, dur, locked }` for a programme card…). These are the painters with the HTML taken out; a row has exactly the fields its row component declares. - `game/actions.js`: every handler as a pure function `(save, ui, …) → { save, ui, toast }`. Nothing in it touches the page; the graph writes what comes back into the stores. - `game/save.js`: `state.js`'s fresh / mend / round-1 import, without localStorage (the store persists itself). - `tools/check-views.mjs` runs every view and action in Node for seasons 1–5 in both languages, including a played gala, and reports any word key that has no row. It found nothing missing, which surprised me; the extraction had kept the keys' shape. - **Didn't map cleanly:** the stage plan was an SVG with draggable circles. NodeGX has no SVG node for that, so `view/formation.js` computes each dancer's place in **pixels** on a 340 px plan and the graph will draw it with absolutely-positioned Groups inside **Drag** nodes. The ruler (a draggable, rotatable SVG ruler) is the one thing I chose not to rebuild; the metre marks along the plan's edges stay. ### 5. The 3D view and the music: `world.js`, `people.js`, `play.js`, `music.js` → `scripts/stage/*.js` - **Was:** modules that import three.js, read the global `G` every frame, find `#gl` in the page, and draw their textures on `document.createElement('canvas')`. - **Became:** the same code as factories, generated by `tools/sync-stage.mjs`: `exports.create(env)` receives three.js, the window and a `G` of its own. The texture canvases became `OffscreenCanvas` (never on the page), and the renderer makes its own canvas, which the "3D stage" Function puts into its Group — the only element any code places. `scripts/stage/stage.js` is the hand-written glue that was `main.js` plus the camera/run half of `ui.js`. The graph calls `sync(save, ui)` whenever a store changes; the stage answers through `emit()`: the live evening four times a second, a tap that places a piece of furniture, the camera's state, where the floating toolbar should be. - **Didn't map cleanly:** `G` was shared by the sheet and the 3D. Now there are two copies: the graph's (the stores) and the stage's, refreshed by `sync()`. The stage never changes the save itself: a tap that places a bench is sent to the graph as `place`, which runs the same action a button would. ### 6. The row components (`UI/*`): the string helpers of `ui.js` - **Was:** helpers returning HTML strings: `stepper()`, the programme `.card`, `.cat` buttons, chips with `aria-pressed`, `.facts` lists, `.meter`s, shop `row()`s, verdict `card()`s with `
`, the step-by-step list. - **Became:** 25 small components, each a Component Inputs → a few Groups and Texts → Component Outputs (its click). Every "pressed / locked / done / now" look is a **States** node driven by a **Boolean To String**, so there is no colour logic in code: `UI/Chip`, `UI/ItemButton`, `UI/Fact`, `UI/Stepper`, `UI/OrderCard`, `UI/ShopRow`, `UI/Meter`, `UI/Swatch`, `UI/FeedLine`, `UI/SumLine`, `UI/PtsItem`, `UI/KcalRow`, `UI/NoteEntry`, `UI/LiveCard`, `UI/GoButton`, `UI/StepChip`, `UI/ChainChip`, `UI/TryStep`, `UI/TryBlock` (a Repeater of TrySteps), `UI/Verdict` (a **Switch** opens the "Why?" sum, a Repeater of SumLines), `UI/HairRow` (a Repeater of Chips that re-publishes the picked one), `UI/DancerDot` (a **Drag** node), `UI/PlanMark`, `UI/MusicSeg`. - **Clicks:** a row publishes `click`; the Repeater re-publishes it with the row's id; a **Send Event** on the channel `gala-act` carries `act` + `arg` to one place that does the work (see the dispatcher below). I proved this chain with a three-chip test page before building on it. - **Got wrong:** my first Chip used an Expression for "locked dims it" — the server counts an Expression as code, so I replaced it with a second States node. A hidden dot still took space (`visible` hides, `mounted` removes), and a width wired as a number inside a row became a flex share, not a percentage (the server warned; the bar is now a column). ### 7. The grown-ups' changes on the backend (new) - **Backend:** a local NodeGX backend with one collection, `GameChange` (`table`, `rowId`, `fields` as JSON text). Anyone may read it (the game must, before it starts); nobody may write it directly. - **Cloud functions** (`#__cloud__/…`), each a Request → nodes → Response graph: - `claimGrownup`: the first signed-in account becomes the home's grown-up (role `grownup`); after that every other account is refused, a child's included. - `saveChange`: Get User Roles (must be `grownup`) → Query Records → a Function holding the checker → Create Record or Update Record. A change is laid over what that row already had, then checked as a whole. - `removeChange`: takes a change back (the row returns to how the game ships it). - **Checked over HTTP**, not just deployed: a child's account gets `notGrownup`; "M3RDE", ``, 100 000 stars, an unknown field and a made-up table are refused with a reason; a good change is saved and a second one merges into it. - **Got wrong, and it mattered:** the backend starts in *dev-open* mode, where permission rules are reported but not enforced — my "nobody may write" rule let a child's account write 9 999 stars straight into the collection. I wrote the rules into `app/nodegx.security.json` (dev-open off, function call rules `role:grownup`), installed them into the backend and restarted it; the same direct write is now `Permission denied`, and so is a child calling `saveChange` at all. The in-graph role check stays as a second lock. ### 8. State and start-up: `state.js` + `main.js`'s start → `Logic/Start Up`, two Global Stores, one dispatcher - **Was:** `load()` from localStorage into `G.S`, `save()` after every change, `G` also holding the screen state. - **Became:** - Global Store **`gala`**, persisted (`storageKey: gala-game-v2`), key `save` — the child's save, on this device, as before. I checked persistence across a reload with a two-button test page first. - Global Store **`ui`**, not persisted: `ui` (tab, screen, picks), `live` (the evening as it plays, written four times a second by the 3D stage), `res` (the rules' answer for the evening), `cam`, `float`, `toast`. Splitting `live` from `ui` matters: only the run sheet and the clock subscribe to it, so the tabs don't recompute four times a second. - **`Logic/Start Up`** (in the App, beside the Router): the Words Static Data → a Variable; Query Records on `GameChange` → "Lay the grown-ups' changes over the game" (checks each row again, then gala-rules' `applyRows`, once) → "Open the save" (repairs or creates it — a new school gets the grown-ups' starting stars) → Variable `ready`, which mounts the Game page. A Delay of 4 s lets the game open with the shipped tables if the backend can't be reached. - **`Game/Dispatcher`**: one Receive Event on `gala-act` → one Function (`game/dispatch.js`) → Set Global Store nodes. Every button in every tab is a Send Event with a fixed `act` (`order:up`, `form:addMove`, `go`) and the row's id as `arg`. This is the coded `changed()`, spread out: the graph shows which button sends what. - **Got wrong:** "Open the save" writes the store it reads, and NodeGX stopped it with *Cyclic loop detected*; unticking Run On Value Change for the store input fixed it. A view Function ran once before the save existed and threw; every view now starts with `if (!Inputs.save || !Inputs.save.school) return;`. ### 9. The screen: `index.html` + `ui.js` painters → `Pages/Game` and its sections - `Game/Stage 3D` (the 3D Group and its Functions), `Game/Top Bar`, `Game/Camera Bar`, `Game/Sheet` (tabs row, scrolling body, buttons row), `Game/Toast` (a Switch and a 2.6 s Delay), `Game/Season Letter` (the modal), `Game/Furniture Toolbar` (the coded `#float`, placed by the 3D stage's `float` output), `Game/Live`, `Game/Results`, and the eight tabs `Tabs/Order`, `Formation`, `Gouter`, `Costumes`, `Build`, `Parking`, `Shop`, `Notebook`. Each tab: one Subscribe per store key it needs, one view Function, Texts and Repeaters, and a Send Event per kind of press. The sheet mounts the tab whose `show_` is true. - **Driven like a child arrives** (`drive_page` from the start page, no page named): the season letter, "C'est parti !", every tab, ▼ on a programme card (the order changed), a dress rehearsal (live clock in the top bar), "Aller à la fin", the verdicts and a "Pourquoi ?" opened, back, gala night: **96 ⭐, 30 → 126**, and the notebook's entry. No console errors at the end. - **Didn't map cleanly:** - `confirm()` (delete a block, start again) and `prompt()` (rename a block) are browser dialogs, not elements; they became an inline "are you sure?" box and an inline Text Input, driven by `ui.confirm` / `ui.renaming`. - Drag-to-reorder of programme cards (pointer tracking over `getBoundingClientRect`) — the cards keep their ▲▼ buttons, which the coded game also had; dragging them is gone. The hint now says "move the cards up or down". - The enlarged plan pop-over (`#planpop`, built with `createElement`) and the ruler are not rebuilt. - Sizes: a percentage sent as a string ("48.5%") is refused by a Group's width; it wants a number in the port's unit. Two components had that wrong and the browser console said so. ### 10. The grown-ups' settings page (new): `Pages/Grownups` - **Built from:** a User node, Log In / Sign Up / Log Out, three Cloud Function nodes (`claimGrownup`, `saveChange`, `removeChange`), a Query Records on `GameChange`, a Repeater of `Grownups/Row Editor` (names in both languages, and the table's numbers: difficulty and counts for a step, price and minutes for a costume…), `Grownups/New Step` and `Grownups/New Costume` (Text Inputs and `UI/Labelled Pick` dropdowns — the server refused six hand-copied label+dropdown boxes and asked for one component, rightly), the stars box, and a `Grownups/Words` Static Data. Four small Functions: what the page shows, the change to send (one check run in the browser first so a grown-up hears *why* at once), the stars, and the error sentence. - **Driven from the game's start page:** ⚙︎ → sign in as the test grown-up → "M3RDE" as a step name → refused with the reason, nothing saved → "Plié royal" → *Enregistré ✓* → a new costume "Pirate" → 80 stars for a new school → "Open the game with the changes" → **"Plié royal" is in the step palette, "Pirate" in the costumes**. A fresh browser (nothing in localStorage) opens a school with **80 ⭐**. A second account ("petitmalin") is told it is not the grown-ups' account, and the editor never mounts. - **Why it lasts:** the changes are rows in the backend, laid over gala-rules' tables by `applyRows` each time the game opens. Clearing the browser loses only the child's save; another computer reading the same backend sees the same changes; a new version of the game ships new default tables and the same rows are laid over them (a row whose id the new version no longer knows is refused by the checker and simply skipped). - **Didn't map cleanly:** a Repeater re-publishes a row's value outputs, but the value it holds is the last row that *changed* one, not the row whose button was pressed — so typing in row A then saving row B would have sent A's text with B's id. The row now packs its own values into one object at the moment its Save is pressed. And the Log Out node's trigger is called `login` (the server said so). ### 11. Clean-up after testing My tests left three accounts and three changes in the backend. I took the changes back through `removeChange`, took the test account out of the `grownup` role, and gave the three test accounts long random passwords nobody knows (the backend has no delete-user tool I could reach). Nobody holds the `grownup` role now: **the first account the real grown-up creates on the settings page becomes the grown-ups' account** — do that before the children find the ⚙︎. --- ## At the end ### What was easy - **The rules.** They were already pure, so "convert" meant a 30-line copier and an equality check. - **Rows → Repeaters.** Every `.map(...).join('')` in `ui.js` became a For Each over the same rows, and the 25 row components were quick once `UI/Chip` had settled the pattern (Component Inputs → States → Component Outputs). - **State.** A persisted Global Store *is* the localStorage save, with change notification for free. - **One dispatcher.** Send Event (`act`, `arg`) from every button into one Receive Event made 60-odd different presses manageable, and it reads well on the canvas. - **The server.** Every refused write named the port, the reason and usually the fix. I never had a write silently accepted that then didn't work, except the dimension-as-string case (caught by the console). ### What was hard - **Volume.** `ui.js` is 752 dense lines; as nodes it is 54 components and 762 nodes. Each tab is one large `create_component` call of 30–90 nodes, and a big page has to be resent whole to change it. - **Things a string of HTML does for free:** the SVG stage plan (now Groups placed in pixels plus Drag nodes), `
` (a Switch), `` in a sentence (dropped), `confirm()`/`prompt()` (inline boxes), `scrollIntoView` on the step being danced (not rebuilt). - **Two copies of state.** The 3D code wants to read the state every frame; the graph wants to own it. `sync()` in, `emit()` out works, but it is the one seam where a bug could hide. - **Security defaults.** The backend started in dev-open mode; a "nobody may write" rule wasn't enforced until I switched enforcement on. Without testing the direct write over HTTP I would have shipped it open. - **Speed in the test browser.** In the headless browser (software WebGL, no GPU) each tap takes 3–7 s to settle; JavaScript is only ~5 ms a frame, the rest is the 3D scene drawn without a GPU. The coded game draws the same scene. I couldn't measure on real hardware from here. ### What was lost or changed - Lost: bold words inside sentences; dragging programme cards (the ▲▼ buttons remain); the ruler and the enlarged stage plan; scrolling the try-out list to the step being danced; the bottom-sheet layout on narrow screens (the sheet stays a 400 px side panel); `window.__game`, the coded game's handle for its own test driver; the import of a round-1 save from another origin. - Changed: the programme hint says "move the cards up or down"; renaming a block and the two confirmations are inline; the school name is checked like a grown-up's name (a rude name is refused with a toast). - Added: the grown-ups' settings, the backend, the checker in two places, the ⚙︎ in the top bar. - Fonts: as before, Fredoka/Nunito/Playball come from Google Fonts when online; offline the system fonts take over. ### How much is nodes, how much is code Counted from the project files (`components/**/nodes.json`, `scripts/**`): | | count | |---|---| | components | 54 (UI 26, Tabs 8, Game 11, Grownups 5, Logic 1, pages 2, cloud functions 3) | | nodes | **762**, of which 363 draw (Group, Text, controls, Repeaters…) and 74 are Send Events | | code nodes | **33** Function nodes (no Expression, no Script node) — 4.3 % of the nodes; the server's own measure says "95.1 % known" | | lines inside those Functions | 390, most of them `Outputs.x = v.x` lines handing rows to Repeaters, plus the ~200-line checker pasted into `saveChange` | | script files | 21 files, 3 369 lines: **2 112 are generated copies** (gala-rules 990, the 3D/music modules 1 014, the checker 108) and **1 257 hand-written** (view rows 585, actions/dispatch/save/text 462, the 3D glue 189, settings 21) | So: every screen, tab, list, button, label, dialog, message and the game's state are nodes; the code is the rules (unchanged), the 3D view and the music (the reference's own modules), and the layer that turns the save into rows and a press into a new save. The words are data in two Static Data nodes (389 game rows, 66 grown-up rows). ### How to see it `npx @nodegx/preview app --open` (from this folder) — it starts the game's backend too. The game opens on the season's letter; the grown-ups' settings are behind ⚙︎ in the top bar. `node tools/check-rules.mjs` and `node tools/check-views.mjs` re-check the code layers; `node tools/sync-rules.mjs` / `sync-stage.mjs` / `sync-check.mjs` regenerate the copies when gala-rules or the checker changes.

content.text:
The game is rebuilt as a NodeGX app in `app/`, and the grown-ups' settings are added. I drove it in the headless browser, starting from the start page each time: every tab, a rehearsal, a try-out, gala night (30 → 126 ⭐ and a notebook entry), buying a costume, placing furniture by tapping the 3D floor, season 2 with its car-park tab, and English. The last runs showed no console errors. The project validator reports 0 errors; 9 of its 12 style warnings are still there and don't affect how it works. The gala-rules tests pass (19/19).

**Do this first:** open the grown-ups' page (⚙︎ in the top bar) and create the grown-ups' account before the kids find it. The first account made there becomes the grown-ups' account, and every account after it is refused. A second account I created as a test was turned away, and the editor never appeared for it.

To play: `npx @nodegx/preview app --open`. It starts the game's backend too.

**The grown-ups' settings**
- Grown-ups can rename a step or change its difficulty, change prices and costume times, rename dances, set a new school's starting stars, and add a new step or costume.
- Changes are kept on the game's backend, not in the browser. A fresh browser opened a school with the grown-ups' 80 stars, and the renamed "Plié royal" and the new "Pirate" costume appeared in the game.
- Changes take effect the next time the game opens. A school already being played keeps its own stars; "Recommencer" in the Carnet starts a new one with the grown-ups' stars.
- **"On another computer" only works if that computer can reach the same backend.** Right now it runs on this machine at `127.0.0.1`, so it's reachable only from here until it's hosted somewhere others can reach.

**Kid safety**
- Every change goes through a check on the server. It accepts only known tables and fields, keeps numbers within ranges, and allows names only as short, plain text that passes a French/English rude-word filter. "M3RDE", HTML and 100 000 stars were all refused over HTTP.
- The browser runs the same check again before applying any change, and the school name a child types is checked the same way.
- One thing I got wrong and fixed: the backend started in a development mode that didn't enforce its permissions. A child's account could write 9 999 stars straight into the database. I switched enforcement on (rules in `app/nodegx.security.json`), and that same write is now refused.

**Nodes and code**
- Every screen, tab, list, button, dialog, the words and the game's state are nodes: 54 components and 762 nodes, of which 33 are Function nodes.
- What stays code (3,369 lines in project scripts):
  - copies made by small generators in `tools/`: gala-rules (with only the import/export lines rewritten, checked to play identical evenings), the 3D and music modules from `reference/`, and the safety checker;
  - about 1,250 hand-written lines that turn the save into the rows the lists show and a button press into a new save.
- Nothing from `reference/`'s page or screen modules is loaded. The only page element any code places is the 3D canvas itself.

**What changed or was lost**
- Gone: bold words inside sentences, dragging the programme cards (the ▲▼ buttons remain), the ruler and the enlarged stage plan, auto-scrolling to the step being danced in a try-out, and the bottom-sheet layout on narrow screens.
- The browser's confirm and prompt pop-ups became boxes inside the sheet.
- In the test browser, which has no graphics card, each tap takes 3–7 s to settle. JavaScript is only about 5 ms per frame; the rest is the 3D scene drawn in software, which the original game would suffer the same way. I couldn't measure it on real hardware.

My test changes are removed from the backend and the three test accounts can no longer sign in, but they couldn't be deleted from here. `CONVERSION.md` has the full log, written as I went.
